disease.name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
disease.description: A progressive fibrotic lung disease used here as a public-data demonstration scenario.

support: Strong mechanistic association with fibroblast activation and extracellular-matrix deposition.
Expression and pathway evidence support a role in fibrotic remodeling.
Potential for differentiated, tissue-focused intervention strategies.
contradictions: Limited late-stage human clinical validation for direct IL11 pathway inhibition.
Translation from preclinical fibrosis models remains an evidence gap.
experiments: Validate target engagement in human IPF precision-cut lung slices.
Compare fibroblast-selective versus systemic pathway inhibition.
Assess translational biomarkers linked to matrix remodeling.

citations.title: Curated public literature set: IL11 and fibrosis

support: Central regulator of fibrotic signaling and extracellular-matrix production.
Extensive literature and pathway evidence across fibrotic diseases.
Multiple intervention strategies demonstrate target relevance.
contradictions: Broad pathway inhibition may create immune, repair, and homeostasis liabilities.
Differentiation is challenging because the pathway is heavily investigated.
experiments: Test localized delivery to reduce systemic pathway suppression.
Identify response biomarkers that separate anti-fibrotic activity from immune effects.
Evaluate combination strategies with approved anti-fibrotic therapy.

citations.title: Curated public literature set: TGF-beta and IPF

support: Single-cell and expression studies associate SPP1-positive macrophage states with fibrosis.
Connects inflammatory cell states to fibroblast activation and tissue remodeling.
contradictions: Causal contribution may differ across disease stages and macrophage subsets.
Direct intervention strategy and patient-selection approach need validation.
experiments: Map SPP1-positive macrophage abundance across disease stages.
Test macrophage-fibroblast co-culture response to pathway inhibition.
Evaluate SPP1 as a pharmacodynamic and patient-stratification biomarker.

citations.title: Curated public literature set: SPP1 macrophages and fibrosis

support: Strong human genetic association with IPF susceptibility.
Biological relevance to airway mucus and epithelial homeostasis.
High value for patient stratification and disease-biology research.
contradictions: Strong association does not automatically imply that direct inhibition is therapeutic.
Mucosal defense and epithelial function create tractability and safety concerns.
compounds: No direct clinical compound included in this curated demo
experiments: Separate causal disease mechanisms from risk-marker utility.
Evaluate genotype-specific epithelial phenotypes in human organoids.
Assess biomarker and stratification value before direct-target investment.
